【P1｜Mr. Utterson】
别称：Utterson
当前一句话身份：Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
档案（最新）：occupation：lawyer；personality：blameless past, troubled by old sins；situation：obsessed with finding and seeing Hyde；residence：bachelor house near a church；identity：lawyer of Gaunt Street
关系：Mr. Richard Enfield（cousin）、Dr. Jekyll（friend）、Dr. Lanyon（friend）、Sir Danvers Carew（lawyer who identifies him）、Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard（police officer assisting him）
至今经历（按时间）：
- Enfield points his cane at a sinister door and asks Utterson if he ever remarked it.
- Enfield calls the door place Black Mail House and muses.
- Utterson asks the name of the man who walked over the child.
- Utterson says he already knows the other party's name.
- Enfield and Utterson agree never to refer to the matter again.
- Utterson comes home in low spirits and studies Jekyll's will in his business room.
- The will leaves all Jekyll's possessions to Edward Hyde, and Hyde inherits if Jekyll vanishes.
- Utterson calls the will madness and now fears it is disgrace.
- Utterson goes to Cavendish Square to consult his friend Dr. Lanyon.
- Utterson asks whether he and Lanyon are Jekyll's two oldest friends.
- Utterson asks Lanyon about Hyde, and Lanyon has never heard of him.
- Utterson lies awake all night, haunted by Enfield's tale and the faceless figure.
- Utterson keeps watch by the by-street door at all hours until his patience is rewarded.
- Utterson resolves to hunt for Hyde, thinking 'If he be Mr. Hyde, I shall be Mr. Seek.'
- A small plainly dressed man approaches the door with a key, and Utterson accosts him as Mr. Hyde.
- Utterson accosts Hyde and asks to be admitted to see Jekyll.
- Utterson asks to see Hyde's face and studies it.
- Hyde angrily accuses Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description.
- Utterson walks away deeply disturbed by Hyde's appearance.
- Poole tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll has gone out.
- Poole confirms Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door.
- Poole says all servants have orders to obey Hyde.
- Poole says Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory.
- Utterson goes home fearing Jekyll is in deep waters.
- Utterson stays behind after Jekyll's dinner to speak with him.
- Utterson raises the subject of Jekyll's will.
- Utterson says he has learned something of young Hyde.
- Utterson offers to help Jekyll out of the matter in confidence.
- Jekyll asks Utterson to help Hyde for his sake when he is gone.
- Utterson promises to bear with Hyde and get his rights for him.
- A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson is found on the victim.
- Utterson identifies the body as Sir Danvers Carew.
- The officer narrates the maid's account and shows the broken stick.
- Utterson recognizes the stick as one he gave Henry Jekyll.
- Utterson offers to take the officer to Hyde's house.
- The old woman lets Utterson and the inspector search Hyde's rooms.
- They find the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book.

别称：Edward Hyde、Hyde、Mr. Hyde、one Hyde、poor Hyde、the fugitive

- The doctor turns sick and white with desire to kill the prisoner.
- They threaten scandal and force the man to pay a hundred pounds.
- The man leads them to the door, unlocks it, and returns with gold and a cheque.
- The man offers to stay until the banks open and cash the cheque himself.
- They spend the night in Enfield's chambers and go to the bank next day.
- The will leaves all Jekyll's possessions to Edward Hyde, and Hyde inherits if Jekyll vanishes.
- Utterson asks Lanyon about Hyde, and Lanyon has never heard of him.
- A small plainly dressed man approaches the door with a key, and Utterson accosts him as Mr. Hyde.
- Utterson accosts Hyde and asks to be admitted to see Jekyll.
- Hyde tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll is from home.
- Utterson asks to see Hyde's face and studies it.
- Hyde gives Utterson his address in Soho.
- Hyde angrily accuses Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description.
- Hyde snarls, unlocks the door, and disappears into the house.
- Jekyll says he takes a great interest in poor Hyde.
- The maid sees Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane.
- The inspector finds several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank.
- The inspector plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.
- Mr. Hyde had few familiars and was hard to trace.
- The maid's master had seen Hyde only twice.
- Hyde's family could not be traced anywhere.
- Hyde had never been photographed.
- Those who could describe Hyde differed widely.
- Observers agreed only on a sense of unexpressed deformity in Hyde.

[note_g1]
Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield。Mr. Utterson is a Gaunt Street lawyer, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. After Enfield showed him a sinister door and named its user, Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, watched the by-street door, and accosted Hyde. Later he stayed after Jekyll's dinner and promised to help Hyde for Jekyll's sake. He then identified Sir Danvers Carew's body and searched Hyde's rooms. He is now obsessed with finding and seeing Hyde.

[note_g2]
Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir。Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, connoisseur, and friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon. He is large, well-made, smooth-faced, with a slyish cast, showing capacity and kindness and warm affection for Utterson. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. After dinner with Utterson, Jekyll refused to hear more of Hyde, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He is now painfully situated, his position strange and not mended by talking.

[note_g3]
Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque。Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, living in Soho and served by Poole and an old woman landlady. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred, impressing beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque. Utterson later accosted him at the by-street door, and Hyde gave his Soho address before disappearing inside. Jekyll called him poor Hyde and asked Utterson to help him. The maid then saw Hyde beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He is now a fugitive with few acquaintances and no traceable family.

[note_g4]
Police officer investigating the murder。Inspector Newcomen is a Scotland Yard officer investigating the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, working with Mr. Utterson, who guides the investigation. He is a professional police officer. He narrated the maid's account and showed the broken stick. Utterson took him to Hyde's house, where the old woman let them search and they found the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book. He found several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank. He now plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.

[note_g5]
Murder victim, an aged gentleman。Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

[note_g6]
Witness who sees Hyde murder Carew。The maid servant is a servant who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew by Edward Hyde. She is a maid servant. She saw Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane. She fainted at the horror of the murder. She woke at two and called the police.
